methodology: Private static inspection of captured module exports, direct calls, function arguments, and JSX DOM wrappers. Resource references are archive-local ordinals. No captured JavaScript or user data is published.

stages.description: The conversation page reads selected conversation state and invokes the turn preparation layer. A branch-preview path can substitute a selected prompt message identity when requesting a separate rendered-turn derivation.

A captured render derivation builds turn entries and per-turn item arrays from conversation-message data. Its item classification includes user and assistant text, reasoning groups, tool activity, generated media, and status-sensitive entries. Its output is not a direct DOM tree.

The turn preparer may append a temporary user-message turn from a pending prompt and attachments. The guard considers active streaming and whether an equivalent pending attachment-bearing turn is already represented.

A turn configuration function maps derived entries to display props, identifies the most recent turn, limits pending/error/feedback props to appropriate turns, applies timestamp separation, and conditionally removes a first user item when hideInitialUserMessage is enabled.

The main conversation page passes renderedTurns and per-turn presentation controls into the exported turn-configuration function. The page also uses the derived conversation representation to manage a local shared conversation state projection.
The exported turn renderer reads turn.items, dispatches item kinds to user, assistant, tool, and media presentation branches, and supplies a wrapper that accepts each rendered item's children.

A nested wrapper emits message-role and source-message identifier attributes for user/assistant/generated-image items. It uses a different lightweight identifier wrapper for other item types and a separate telemetry wrapper.

visual_semantics: The main display model is an ordered set of turns whose items may represent multiple source messages rather than one DOM element per mapping node.
A temporary pending submission can appear as a user turn before a server-backed message is available.
The first user item can be hidden by an explicit presentation option without asserting any deletion from the underlying conversation mapping.
Role and source-message attributes on rendered elements are a DOM identification mechanism, not proof of original message text or storage keys.
unverified: The visible main-page to typed-turn-renderer import is verified; other dynamic subcomponent imports and hidden rendering branches are not exhaustively mapped.
Visibility rules for every item kind, safety presentation, streaming placeholders, and hidden content remain to be enumerated.

Turn-level virtualization, keyed row placement, measured scroll anchoring, and the voice spacer are source-reviewed separately. React reconciliation, hydration, and actual browser scroll outcomes are still unverified.
These source render paths were not executed against a live site or real user data.
The complete click-to-network action path for each edit/fork/regenerate control remains distinct from these verified renderer callback bindings.
confidentiality: No captured source snippets, original filenames, message text, account identities, URLs, tokens or raw event bodies are included.

verified_cross_module_call.behavior: A conversation page turn-entry component imports the exported typed turn renderer and passes the configured turn, conversation identity, current-turn flag, presentation flags and action callbacks.
verified_cross_module_call.boundary: The imported module and JSX invocation are visible. Page mount conditions, actual loaded chunks, scrolling, and runtime visibility have not been observed.

presentation_rules.description: A temporary user turn is omitted when there is no pending prompt, when active streaming makes a text-empty prompt unsuitable, or when a matching attachment-bearing pending turn is already represented.
Pending-loading presentation is requested when a synthetic pending turn exists, or while streaming when no existing derived turn already contains an in-progress item.
A hide-first-user option removes user-message items from the first displayed turn's items without modifying the original conversation mapping.
The final displayed turn receives pending attachments, last-turn errors and request-input indicators; earlier turns receive separate display flags and timestamp delimiters.
Under a conditional alternate-prompt presentation, the page derives rendered turns using a specified prompt message as the selected node instead of the ordinary prepared current-node path.
A special sidebar mode or a locally blocked moderation condition enters a simplified item-classification path rather than the regular item decomposition.

Reasoning recaps, tool results, generated images, moderation notices, message fragments and streaming-related statuses have conditional grouping or presentation treatment; no universal visibility claim is inferred.
User, assistant and generated-image items are assigned role/source-message identification attributes and test selectors where available; tool and other items can use different lightweight wrappers.
A separate rendering telemetry wrapper receives item-scoped telemetry messages around the display children; the telemetry wrapper is not evidence of an additional conversation message.

rule_limitations: The filter options describe a client rendering choice and do not establish deletion from stored message mapping.
Status-dependent or moderation-dependent code paths may be gated by runtime settings and have not been exercised.
These nine rules are individually inspected examples, not an exhaustive truth table of all possible item types and rendering modes.

action_bindings.gates: Requires a user-message item, the eligible message identity, an available edit callback, and absence of certain targeted-reply or unsupported attachment conditions.
action_bindings.limits: An eligible edit callback is source-visible, not an observed edit or persisted rewrite.

action_bindings.gates: Regeneration callbacks can be disabled by read-only presentation, pending-alternative state, and model-first-landing or other special-turn conditions.
action_bindings.limits: This captures callback availability and gating; actual regeneration request construction is researched separately.

action_bindings.gates: The renderer forwards a supplied fork callback into its turn-actions layer, which can be independently suppressed for particular presentation states.
action_bindings.limits: The turn renderer's callback forwarding does not by itself prove the downstream branch request executed.

observations: The page selects the active mapping and current node from either ordinary scoped conversation state or a reviewed/alternate conversation state.
It constructs memoized turn-derivation arguments with explicit threadMapping and threadCurrentNode fields.
The memoized calculation dependency checks include the current-node and mapping references, so changing either participates in recomputation.
The page passes the resulting renderedTurns to its later per-turn display stage.
A conditional effect sets or clears a separate shared-conversation projection for qualifying work-conversation state.
page_recomputation.boundary: Captured React compiler memo-cache comparisons and source assignments are visible; the render timing, component mount, React reconciliation and a user's observed branch-switch effect are not verified.

viewport_windowing_followup.relationship: The conversation page renders derived turns through an imported virtualized turn window. A separate response spacer controls placement and scroll compensation.
